alalal-c44613-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 6: whether God is in things in many ways, differently in the temple, in heaven and in the soul.

alalal-c44613-d1e117.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's phrase about those whom God makes his most beloved temple.

alalal-c44613-d1e129.summary: Proposes that God is in things in many ways: differently in heaven, in the temple, in other places, and in the just soul.

alalal-c44613-d1e141.summary: Solution: Albert concedes that God is in different things in many ways and, following the saints, enumerates them: in heaven as where his works of glory shine, in the world as creator and governor, in the angel as savour and beauty, in the Church as father of the household, in the faithful soul as bridegroom in the chamber; everywhere by essence conserving, by power governing, by presence knowing; in the just by indwelling grace; in the sacraments by efficacy; in the dove, breath and tongues of fire as mystery and sign; in the temple as place of propitiation (Genesis 28); in the whole Christ by union, and with the soul alone in hell and the body alone in the tomb. Many other modes can be found by reflection.
claims: God is present in creatures in many diverse modes, differentiated by effect and relation.

alalal-c44613.summary: Article 6, prompted by Lombard's reference to the saints as God's beloved temple, asks whether God is in things in many ways. Albert concedes that he is and, drawing on the saints, catalogues the modes. God is in heaven as where his glory shines, in the world as creator and governor, in angels as savour and beauty, in the Church as head of the household, and in the faithful soul as bridegroom. He is everywhere by essence, power and presence; in the just by grace; in the sacraments by efficacy; in theophanic signs by mystery; in the temple as the place of propitiation; and in Christ by union, including his union with the separated soul in hell and the body in the tomb. The list is open-ended.
claims: God is present in creatures in many modes, distinguished by his different effects and relations.
